annotations.annotation_text: The exit warning from the Museyroom. This mirrors the entry warning on page 8, framing the entire Wellington passage as an enclosed, subterranean visit to the crypt of history.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: A reference to the Puck of A Midsummer Night's Dream, or the Irish Púca. The mischievous spirit that scrambles the historical narrative, leaving the visitor confused by the tour.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: A 'farrago' or confused mixture. This perfectly describes the Museyroom's collection of historical detritus, and by extension, the linguistic method of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: The final payment or 'tip' to Kate the guide. The economic transaction concludes the tour, reducing the epic history to a cheap, paid amusement park attraction.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: The knapsack of the departing soldier or the bag in which the museum visitor carries away their confused memories. It hints at theft ('nab') of historical truth.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: The exit gate of Phoenix Park or the museum. Passing through the gate signifies the end of this specific vignette and the transition to the next dream-layer of the Wake.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: A papal bull or a Roman amulet. Authority—religious or imperial—is stamped on the departing visitor, concluding the Theocratic phase's obsession with monumental edicts.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/

annotations.annotation_text: A subtle prompt pointing toward the ultimate awakening of Finnegan. Even in the depths of the museum-crypt, the possibility of resurrection (the core theme of the Wake) is planted.
sources: FWEET: Finnegans Wake Extensible Elucidation Treasury. http://fweet.org/
